25e5215eb24a.criterion: Clearing the shared commit slab on closing a NULL graph/submodule repo discards data still needed by the parent; that close must leave the slab intact.
source: commit-graph: move slab-clearing to close_commit_graph()

The bug is in step (2) above. We should not be clearing the slab when
cleaning up the submodule repository structs. Prior to ac6d45d11f, we
did not do so because it was done inside a helper function that returned
early when it saw NULL. So the behavior change from that commit is that
we'll now _always_ clear the slab via repo_clear(), even if the
repository being closed did not have a commit graph (and thus would have
a NULL commit_graph struct).
25e5215eb24a.answer: The earlier decision to move slab-clearing to `close_commit_graph()` now fails because the commit introduces a scenario where the slab is cleared even when the repository does not have a commit graph struct, as seen with the observed condition of `ac6d45d11f`.

2cee4b76215e.criterion: The other decision closes an unused file descriptor after mmap to avoid fd exhaustion; it does not release the shared graph slab.
source: commit-graph: move slab-clearing to close_commit_graph()

The bug is in step (2) above. We should not be clearing the slab when
cleaning up the submodule repository structs. Prior to [ref], we
did not do so because it was done inside a helper function that returned
early when it saw NULL. So the behavior change from that commit is that
we'll now _always_ clear the slab via repo_clear(), even if the
repository being closed did not have a commit graph (and thus would have
a NULL commit_graph struct).

We don't ever refer to the descriptor after mmap-ing it. And keeping it
open means we can run out of descriptors in degenerate cases (e.g.,
thousands of split chain files). Let's close it as soon as possible.
2cee4b76215e.answer: The other decision addresses closing file descriptors immediately after use, whereas the incoming report discusses avoiding slab clearing in certain repository cleanup scenarios.

4c33ac7b48ab.criterion: The refactored reverse-index writer needlessly allocates/sorts pack order when no .rev will be written; skip this work on that path.
source:
Prepare for the multi-pack index to write a .rev file by providing a way
to write the reverse index without an array of pack_idx_entry (which the
MIDX code does not have).

Fix a performance regression introduced in a587b5a786 (pack-write.c:
extract 'write_rev_file_order', 2021-03-30) and stop needlessly
allocating the "pack_order" array and sorting it with
"pack_order_cmp()", only to throw that work away when we discover that
we're not writing *.rev files after all.
4c33ac7b48ab.answer: The earlier decision to prepare for writing a .rev file by allocating and sorting the "pack_order" array appears flawed given the report revealing we are no longer writing *.rev files, necessitating a recheck of this assumption.

4f4df9b7e8a6.criterion: Progress output added for commit-graph writes fails to honor --quiet and must be suppressed then.
source:
Furthermore, since the gc.writeCommitGraph setting was added in
d5d5d7b641 ("gc: automatically write commit-graph files", 2018-06-27),
there was no indication at all from a "git gc" run that anything was
different. This why one of the progress bars being added here uses
start_progress() instead of start_delayed_progress(), so that it's
guaranteed to be seen. E.g. on my tiny 867 commit dotfiles.git
repository:

Fix a regression in my recent 7b0f229222 ("commit-graph write: add
progress output", 2018-09-17).  The newly added progress output for
"commit-graph write" didn't check the --quiet option.
4f4df9b7e8a6.answer: The original author should revisit the decision to add progress output for "commit-graph write" without checking the --quiet option, as revealed by the reported regression in 7b0f229222 (\"commit-graph write: add progress output\", 2018-09-17).

f1725f7b6fb6.criterion: Adding scalar to the command-documentation regex shifted the man-section capture from $1 to $2 (or captured the name instead of the section).
source:
Add 'scalar' as a 'mainporcelain' command in the Git command list. Update
the regex in 'cmd-list.perl' used to match the first line of command
documentation to find 'scalar(1)'.

We attribute each documentation text file to a man section by finding a
line in the file that looks like "gitfoo(<digit>)". Commit [ref]
("[referenced subject]", 2022-09-02) updated this
logic to look not only for "gitfoo" but also "scalarfoo". In doing so,
it forgot to account for the fact that after the updated regex has found
a match, the man section is no longer to be found in `$1` but now lives
in `$2`.
f1725f7b6fb6.answer: The original author's update to the regex for matching man sections in Git documentation commands failed to correctly handle the new structure where the man section is now located in `$2` instead of `$1`.
